question: True or false: ripe tomatoes kept a week in the fridge lose aroma that days back at room temperature do not fully restore?
answer: True. In a 2016 University of Florida study, ripe tomatoes held at 5 °C for a week lost many of the volatile compounds that carry their aroma. After three days back at 20 °C, several had not returned. The cold switches off genes that make those compounds, and not all switch back on.
move: Storage that preserves one quality can quietly destroy another.
ask: Is there something I protect in a way that keeps it safe but spoils what I love about it?
trap: Cold keeps everything fresh, so the fridge must keep it at its best.
reference: Zhang, Wang, Tieman et al., Chilling-induced tomato flavor loss is associated with altered volatile synthesis and transient changes in DNA methylation, PNAS, 2016
